subject: trumpetfish
title: This Fish Hunts by Hiding Behind Another Fish. Models Proved It

scenes.text: This hunter's disguise is another fish, swimming beside it.
It's the trumpetfish, a long thin reef predator in the Caribbean. It eats small damselfish.
Damselfish bolt when they see it coming. So it slides up alongside a parrotfish, a harmless plant eater.
Scientists tested it off Curacao, pulling 3D-printed fish past damselfish on nylon lines.
A lone trumpetfish model sent them fleeing. Beside a parrotfish model, they didn't notice it.
It's the only known case of an animal, other than us, using another animal as cover to hunt.

description:
The trumpetfish hunts by swimming right beside another fish and using it as a moving hiding place.
On reefs off Curacao, researchers pulled 3D-printed models past colonies of damselfish. The damselfish fled from a trumpetfish model on its own, but when it was attached beside a model of a plant-eating parrotfish they reacted as they did to the parrotfish alone. The team called it the only known example of a non-human animal using another animal as concealment (Current Biology, August 2023).
Sneakiest predator you know of? Comment below.
first_comment: Divers reported seeing the trick more often on damaged reefs, where there is less coral to hide behind. Clever or just lazy?
